quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (Q1'26 investor-conference deck): net sales NT$49,087 million, up 63.1% QoQ and 582.9% YoY, as ASP increased >70% QoQ (>200% YoY) while bit shipment decreased mid-single digit% QoQ; gross margin 67.9% (Q4'25: 49.0%), operating margin 61.3%, net income NT$26,058 million at a 53.1% net margin, EPS NT$8.41; EBITDA margin 67.2%. Q1'26 CAPEX was NT$2.8B and free cash flow NT$28,740 million; Q1'26 net cash and equivalents NT$68.5B. The deck states accumulated profit of NT$232 billion over 13 years (as of Q1'26) and that the company is expected to self-fund new fab construction.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales NT$49,087 million (+63.1% QoQ, +582.9% YoY); GM 67.9%; net income NT$26,058 million; EPS NT$8.41; Q1'26 CAPEX NT$2.8B

quarterly_data.signal: Company outlook in the Q1'26 deck: Q2'26 expected to further improve beyond Q1'26, and high gross margin sustainable in the next few quarters; Y2026 bit shipment target up teens% YoY with a healthy inventory level.

Nanya's DRAM market outlook (Q2'26) in the deck: AI-driven CSP capex supports strong cloud DRAM demand (HBM / RDIMM / LPDDR5); constrained DDR5, DDR4, LPDDR4 and DDR3 supply leads to legacy DRAM EOL; in 2026 the industry introduces marginal new capacity, focused on high-end CSP and value-added demand; HBM, high-density DDR5 and LPDDR5 lead overall DRAM demand, with strong DDR4, LPDDR4 and DDR5 demand for high-end e-SSD, BMC and NICs; overall demand seen remaining strong, healthy and sustainable. Nanya says its DDR4/LPDDR4 is serving the industry-wide supply gap.

Operation update in the Q1'26 deck: DDR5 contributes 10% of revenue, flexible to increase if needed; customized AI UWIO memory is contributing initial revenue; new fab construction on schedule with a target equipment move-in in Q1'27; 1C/1D/EUV development on schedule.
quarterly_data.figure: DDR5 10% of revenue; new fab equipment move-in target Q1'27

quarterly_data.signal: Four major customers participated in Nanya's private placement (MOPS announcement on March 25, 2026); the deck states the supply agreements include stable supply of multiple product mix, and gives the rationale as strengthening the Nanya-customer partnership and building a win-win position in the AI/CSP supply chain (e-SSD, networking).
